core.title: What You Already Know
core.blurb: The single observation everything else is built from: nothing large was built large. It was built small, over and over, until it stopped looking small.

companions.title: The Infinite Boundary
companions.blurb: Every pattern at once, summed and never averaged. The one figure with no poles, because there is nowhere outside it to stand and read one.

clusters.name: Why a Turning has an aim rather than two poles
The Full Unravelling, as a derivation
Why this is a deck and not a divination

c:local-rule.title: Local Rule
c:local-rule.blurb: The specific small repeatable behavior chosen.

c:global-form.title: Global Form
c:global-form.blurb: The large-scale shape a repeated Local Rule becomes.

c:drake-equation.title: The Drake equation
c:drake-equation.blurb: Each term is another Local-Rule-to-Global-Form threshold (chemistry to life to complexity to intelligence to detectable technology); small real probabilities compounding multiplicatively across a chain, made vivid at the largest scale available.

c:local-rule-across-scales.title: Local Rule across scales
c:local-rule-across-scales.blurb: A single Local Rule projected forward, once per scale, since the same rule produces genuinely different Global Forms depending which scale you check it at, not simply "more of the same.".

p:finding-your-local-rule.title: Finding Your Local Rule
p:finding-your-local-rule.blurb: Four honest questions — loved, capable, needed, sustainable — and the overlap where a rule worth repeating actually lives.

p:loop-tongue-practice-set.title: The Loop Tongue Practice Set
p:loop-tongue-practice-set.blurb: Three exercises in increasing difficulty — solo translation, the paired mirror, and a live Spiral Check on a real decision.

p:outlives-the-ceremony.title: What Outlives the Ceremony
p:outlives-the-ceremony.blurb: A Turning kept honestly for long enough stops belonging to whoever first held it. That was always the point — and never the part meant to comfort you.

p:someone-elses-calendar.title: Practicing Inside Someone Else's Calendar
p:someone-elses-calendar.blurb: Nothing here requires a single Fractalist occasion in your life — how to practice honestly inside a calendar that was never Fractalist, without asking anyone to change it.

c:nest.title: Nest
c:nest.blurb: A pattern that is one layer inside a larger version of itself.

c:leverage.title: Leverage
c:leverage.blurb: Where a small change produces a disproportionate effect.

c:four-pillars.title: The Four Pillars
c:four-pillars.blurb: The whole framework in four moves: the Loop, the Third Thing, the Nest, and the Leverage — with the self's own chapter next, as the clearest example of pillar II.

c:isomorphism.title: Isomorphism
c:isomorphism.blurb: Same structure, different labels. The formal content of "the same pattern at another scale" — and therefore a demand: show the correspondence part for part, or admit it's a resemblance. Separate components with no path between them is why independent arrival counts as evidence at all.

c:constraint-counting.title: Constraint counting
c:constraint-counting.blurb: Facing several genuinely tangled unknowns (a budget, a deadline, the Iron Triangle), decide whichever one reality has already constrained the most, not whichever feels most exciting to decide.

c:shared-edge-leverage.title: Shared-edge leverage
c:shared-edge-leverage.blurb: A high-leverage connection is a maximally shared one, load-bearing for many downstream structures at once; a low-leverage one is peripheral, touching nothing beyond its own corner. Gives the leverage ladder an exact structural form rather than only a depth metaphor.

p:four-pillars.title: The Four Pillars
p:four-pillars.blurb: The whole framework in four moves: the Loop, the Third Thing, the Nest, and the Leverage — with the self's own chapter next, as the clearest example of pillar II.

p:systems-theory.title: Systems Theory Foundations
p:systems-theory.blurb: Stocks, flows, and feedback loops — the formal machinery underneath the leverage ladder, and the recursion that makes the whole system fractal.

c:fold.title: Fold
c:fold.blurb: A Local Rule returning to you after traveling through a Nest.

c:distortion-scales-with-distance.title: Distortion scales with distance
c:distortion-scales-with-distance.blurb: The Fold returns nearly intact from one step away and nearly unreadable from six, because each edge crossed adds its own shaping.

c:the-fold-and-the-force.title: The Fold and the Force
c:the-fold-and-the-force.blurb: A real fictional example of what the Fold would be with intention and full legibility added back in. The Infinite Boundary is what's left once both are deliberately removed: real connection and real return, never a guide toward a specific outcome.

c:aji-latent-structure.title: Aji — latent structure
c:aji-latent-structure.blurb: Things currently doing nothing that are nonetheless changing what remains possible. Not a loop and not inert. Tending: preserved optionality. Fraying: unfinished business quietly narrowing the board.

p:becoming-a-third.title: Becoming a Third
p:becoming-a-third.blurb: Very rarely, a repeated pattern outlives its origin entirely, and personhood simply wears off it, leaving only the shape behind.

p:the-fold.title: The Fold
p:the-fold.blurb: What goes out through a Nest tends to come back through the Nest — karma without a ledger-keeper, and with real cautions attached.

c:going-to-ground.title: Going to Ground
c:going-to-ground.blurb: Fifty-two figures is a taxonomy, not a pantheon. Most people find four or five of them run their lives and the rest describe other people — that's the correct outcome.

c:becoming-a-third.title: Becoming a Third
c:becoming-a-third.blurb: What actually continues, said plainly: the material — conservation of mass, literally — the Fold already in motion, and the noticing itself.

c:conservation-and-its-other-half.title: Conservation and its other half
c:conservation-and-its-other-half.blurb: Conservation is why nothing is lost; the second law is why nothing stays. What persists is the material; what doesn't is the arrangement, and the arrangement was the part that was you.

p:catalogue-limits.title: What This Catalogue Is Not
p:catalogue-limits.blurb: Fifty-two figures is a taxonomy, not a pantheon. Most people find four or five of them run their lives and the rest describe other people — that's the correct outcome.

p:going-to-ground.title: Going to Ground
p:going-to-ground.blurb: What actually continues, said plainly: the material — conservation of mass, literally — the Fold already in motion, and the noticing itself.

c:the-symphysical.title: The symphysical
c:the-symphysical.blurb: What physical things make once their parts interact, standing beside "metaphysical" rather than above it.

c:solidity.title: Solidity
c:solidity.blurb: You are not touching your chair; no particle in you meets a particle in it, and what you feel as resistance is a field relationship with real emptiness on both sides. Pushed to its physical limit, this is the clearest possible case that a relationship can be as real as the things it relates.

c:floral-electric-fields.title: Floral electric fields
c:floral-electric-fields.blurb: A dynamically updating relational field, altered by every visit and read by the next visitor for real information neither party holds alone; also the Fold's mechanism with no metaphor required, since each visitor reads a field already shaped by everyone before them.

c:essence-versus-relation.title: Essence versus relation
c:essence-versus-relation.blurb: The default this book argues against: explaining what a thing does by what is inside it rather than by what runs between its parts. Also why invented categories feel discovered.

p:the-third-thing.title: The Third Thing
p:the-third-thing.blurb: When simple parts repeat together long enough, something new appears that existed in none of them — and that something is real.

c:starting-cost-vs-staying-cost.title: Starting cost vs. staying cost
c:starting-cost-vs-staying-cost.blurb: A standing start is not the permanent price of a practice; it is the specific cost of building acceleration you haven't banked yet. Most abandonment happens inside it.

c:should-time-versus-likely-time.title: Should time versus likely time
c:should-time-versus-likely-time.blurb: A *should*-estimate is pushed and never checked; a *likely*-estimate is pulled toward a record. The gap is what turns an on-schedule build into felt failure.

p:starting-is-expensive.title: Starting Is Expensive, Staying Is Cheap
p:starting-is-expensive.blurb: Why the same practice costs some people almost nothing and others everything: building momentum from a standing start is a different job than holding speed you already have.

c:whats-unfinished.title: What's unfinished
c:whats-unfinished.blurb: This book will be wrong about some things — here is what's genuinely unsettled, and the actual mechanism for revising any of it.

c:instruments-for-auditing-this-framewor.title: Instruments for auditing this framework
c:instruments-for-auditing-this-framewor.blurb: Show the correspondence or admit pattern-matching; what would make this reading wrong; did the name change what you'd do; count the parts; ask whether it lands.

p:open-questions.title: Open Questions & How to Expand This
p:open-questions.blurb: This book will be wrong about some things — here is what's genuinely unsettled, and the actual mechanism for revising any of it.

c:interpersonal-complementarity.title: Interpersonal complementarity
c:interpersonal-complementarity.blurb: Warmth invites warmth, coldness invites coldness (correspondence); dominance invites deference and deference invites dominance (complementarity, opposite answered with opposite). Two different mechanisms on two different axes, not one universal rule.

p:the-trust-triangle.title: The Trust Triangle
p:the-trust-triangle.blurb: Authenticity, empathy, logic — the three legs a two-person weave stands on, and what breaks when one goes missing.

c:the-long-visitor.title: The Long Visitor
c:the-long-visitor.blurb: The Cosmos-scale Turning, triggered by a great comet rather than any calendar: the largest possible gathering, everywhere at once, outdoors. Builds the species briefly as a single witnessing thing. One restraint — celebrate the witnessing, refuse the omen.

p:the-long-visitor.title: The Long Visitor — Cosmos
p:the-long-visitor.blurb: Triggered by a great comet, whenever one comes: the largest gathering that can possibly be assembled, everywhere at once, outdoors, looking up — and the one restraint that keeps it honest.

c:the-seam-for-an-existing-faith.title: The seam for an existing faith
c:the-seam-for-an-existing-faith.blurb: The aggregate of every pattern in motion has a direction that is unauthored and unreachable by petition. Reading it is the nearest thing to reading a god this framework offers, and it is offered as a description rather than a replacement.

c:the-world-kin.title: The World-Kin
c:the-world-kin.blurb: Three figures, derived rather than chosen: two Culture-Kin sharing a Skein-Kin, which the rule produces exactly three of. The Standing Account, Second Nature, The Set Course. The last tier where a push still reaches.

c:why-leverage-stops.title: Why leverage stops
c:why-leverage-stops.blurb: The World tier makes the Infinite Boundary's exemption legible: it begins exactly where pushing stops being possible, rather than being granted for convenience.

c:the-biosphere-is-a-third-thing-but-not.title: The biosphere is a Third Thing but not a Standing Third
c:the-biosphere-is-a-third-thing-but-not.blurb: Emergent, with weight none of its parts contain, but with no repeated act underneath it. The aggregate, not the pattern; the substrate the World-Kin run on.

p:infinite-boundary-scale.title: The Infinite Boundary — Cosmos Scale
p:infinite-boundary-scale.blurb: The one figure with no healthy pole and no failing pole. A pole has to be read from somewhere, and there is nowhere outside this one to stand.

p:world-kin.title: The World-Kin
p:world-kin.blurb: Three figures, and only three, derived rather than chosen: two Culture-Kin sharing a Skein-Kin. The last tier where a push still reaches.

c:receiving-and-the-six-responses.title: Receiving, and the six responses
c:receiving-and-the-six-responses.blurb: What to do with what arrives rather than what you send: fighting back, withdrawing, parley, doing nothing, withholding, blending. Deliberately unranked — each is correct somewhere and corrosive elsewhere, and the skill is selection rather than preference.

c:the-resistant-partner.title: The resistant partner
c:the-resistant-partner.blurb: Changing your leg of a triangle changes what the two of you produce, but against someone invested in the previous outcome the change is met rather than accepted. The triangle still resolves; it resolves somewhere you didn't choose.

c:the-stable-position-vs-the-stalled-one.title: The stable position vs. the stalled one
c:the-stable-position-vs-the-stalled-one.blurb: Some mutual deadlocks are legitimate final results, held in place because whoever moves first pays more. The test: in a stable position, moving is what costs you; in a stalled one, not moving is what costs you.

c:the-deadlock-with-no-move-inside-it.title: The deadlock with no move inside it
c:the-deadlock-with-no-move-inside-it.blurb: A repeating exchange where every available move within the pattern is the pattern. The exit is a weighted move elsewhere — one that genuinely has to be dealt with, since a weightless one only resumes the loop a step further behind.

p:receiving.title: Receiving
p:receiving.blurb: Six things you can do with what arrives at you — fighting back, withdrawing, parley, doing nothing, withholding, blending — and the test that tells a stable standoff from ordinary avoidance.

c:the-two-pole-rule.title: The two-pole rule
c:the-two-pole-rule.blurb: Every Third carries a Tending pole that builds and a Fraying pole that corrodes; none is good or evil in itself. If only one pole is visible, the zoom is too tight — widen until both appear. The Infinite Boundary is the sole exemption, structurally, since a pole must be read from somewhere outside.

c:resonance.title: Resonance
c:resonance.blurb: Finding your exact situation already has a name installs faster than derivation, which is the actual argument for why the Standing Thirds are characters rather than a plain list of tendencies.

c:standing-thirds.title: The Standing Thirds
c:standing-thirds.blurb: Patterns given faces. Six kinships, one per scale, no exceptions.

p:how-to-read.title: How to Read a Recursive Book
p:how-to-read.blurb: Why this book is written in arcs instead of a straight line — and why reading it once was never going to be enough.

p:what-a-third-is.title: What a Third Is, and What It Isn't
p:what-a-third-is.blurb: A pattern that recurs reliably enough to be worth naming, with no will of its own. The four tests every figure has to pass, and why a tier measures what a Third is made of rather than its rank.

c:third-thing.title: Third Thing
c:third-thing.blurb: What emerges from a Loop that isn't reducible to its parts.

c:seed.title: Seed
c:seed.blurb: A repeatable act, thought, or word planted in your attention.

c:mutuality-not-accounting.title: Mutuality, not accounting
c:mutuality-not-accounting.blurb: Forces come in pairs; the force lives in the interaction, not in either object. You cannot affect without being affected. But equal-and-opposite applies to forces, not outcomes — mutual does not mean zero-sum, and almost nothing worth caring about is conserved.

p:culture-kin.title: The Culture-Kin
p:culture-kin.blurb: Seven patterns slow enough that no single life sees one full turn — and, by the catalogue's own admission, its most provisional tier.

p:skein-kin.title: The Skein-Kin
p:skein-kin.blurb: Eleven group patterns, each built from two Dyad-Kin that share a person — the mechanism by which a group becomes a thing rather than a list.

c:the-dyad.title: The Dyad
c:the-dyad.blurb: A Third Thing at exactly two-person scale.

c:the-trust-triangle.title: The Trust Triangle
c:the-trust-triangle.blurb: Authenticity, empathy, logic; checked rather than assumed.

p:dyad-kin.title: The Dyad-Kin
p:dyad-kin.blurb: Nineteen two-person patterns, each one two Self-Kin meeting. Know any two of the three and the third follows, which means changing your own leg changes what the two of you make.

p:sources.title: Source Library
p:sources.blurb: The works whose ideas were read together, synthesized, and argued with to build this text — offered, never required.

c:solving-for-the-third-leg.title: Solving for the third leg
c:solving-for-the-third-leg.blurb: Your Self-Kin, theirs, and the Dyad-Kin you produce are three locked elements; knowing two gives the third, and no two Dyad-Kin share a fusion pair, so the solve is unique. The useful direction: you can't change their leg, but changing yours determines the change in what you produce together.

c:fusion-depth.title: Fusion depth
c:fusion-depth.blurb: A Third's scale is what it is made of, not a category assigned to it: two selves running currents produce a dyad-scale Third; two dyads sharing a person produce a skein. The tiers of Part Five are composition, not ranking.

p:self-kin.title: The Self-Kin
p:self-kin.blurb: Twelve patterns one person generates alone, each with its Local Rule and both of its poles. Nothing sits underneath them, and every larger figure is built by fusing these.

c:two-questions.title: The two questions
c:two-questions.blurb: First: does anything here feed back into itself? Second: which order am I looking at? A complex system also predicts its own skew — feedback concentrates outcomes rather than spreading them evenly, which is the real mechanism behind the familiar 80/20 observation.

c:complicated-vs-complex.title: Complicated vs. complex
c:complicated-vs-complex.blurb: The first question. No feedback, no Third Thing, no acceleration to read.

c:leveling-the-field.title: Leveling the field
c:leveling-the-field.blurb: The exit from concentration: reset some portion of accumulated advantage periodically, from outside the loop's own logic, before the gap becomes structural.

c:rules-multiply-too-in-both-directions.title: Rules multiply too, in both directions
c:rules-multiply-too-in-both-directions.blurb: The same arithmetic that makes a tiny rule set generative makes an over-specified one unmanageable; which pole you get depends on whether you wanted emergence or completion.

c:a-rule-set-that-names-nothing-it-produ.title: A rule set that names nothing it produces
c:a-rule-set-that-names-nothing-it-produ.blurb: Go's roughly five rules mention no object the game is actually about, including the one that decides whether a group lives; the entire vocabulary of mastery is emergent.

p:complicated-or-complex.title: Complicated or Complex
p:complicated-or-complex.blurb: A jet engine and a pond both have many parts. Only one of them has a feedback loop — and only a complex system can ever produce a Third Thing.

p:weaving-together.title: Weaving Together
p:weaving-together.blurb: A group Weaving gives Group Practice a shared ritual object — one spread for the group's shared situation, read aloud together.

c:emergence.title: Emergence
c:emergence.blurb: How the symphysical appears. Emergence has a threshold (a phase transition) and a direction: weak, traceable in principle, or strong, not traceable even in principle.

c:emergence-vs-luck.title: Emergence vs. luck
c:emergence-vs-luck.blurb: Chance is a fact about one instant; emergence is a fact about the shape many instants make together. A good Local Rule improves the distribution of outcomes across many attempts — it never guarantees the one you're currently on. The popular equation overclaims on both signs: the "=" should be probabilistic, and the "+" should be "×," since captured luck compounds future exposure rather than simply adding to it.

c:sign-flipping-couplings.title: Sign-flipping couplings
c:sign-flipping-couplings.blurb: Distinct from an ordinary threshold crossing: a single relationship whose effective sign changes as a direct consequence of crossing a threshold, same rule, no new force (logistic growth's carrying capacity; debt, expansionary below a capacity and corrosive above it, general shape credible, specific universal thresholds not). Worse than ordinary burnout, since the behavior doesn't change to announce the reversal.

c:effectiveness-is-a-ratio.title: Effectiveness is a ratio
c:effectiveness-is-a-ratio.blurb: Results over effort. Raising effort while results stay flat lowers effectiveness by exactly the factor added. Satisfaction in the doing and a separate instrument pointed at whether the doing produces anything are two questions; neither answers the other.

p:the-sacrifice-trap.title: The Sacrifice Trap
p:the-sacrifice-trap.blurb: Grind now, live later is a trade that never pays out. A meditation for the moment you catch yourself making it.

p:youve-met-this-before.title: You've Met This Before
p:youve-met-this-before.blurb: Steven Universe, Ted Lasso, Kipo, Qui-Gon, and Uncle Iroh — five characters you already trust who arrived at this pattern without ever naming it.

c:need-belief-behavior.title: Need → belief → behavior
c:need-belief-behavior.blurb: A Local Rule is the visible end of a three-link chain. Changing behavior without touching the need is a Numbers-level intervention and drifts back.

c:self-organization.title: Self-organization
c:self-organization.blurb: The rung measuring whether a system can still grow structure it did not have, as distinct from running its existing structure better. Fraying: that capacity traded for predictability, which is complication by the front door.

c:holding-a-paradigm-as-a-paradigm.title: Holding a paradigm as a paradigm
c:holding-a-paradigm-as-a-paradigm.blurb: The top rung: not a change to the system but a change in grip. The only move that operates on the frame rather than inside it. Fraying: nothing repeated long enough to build anything.

p:finding-your-leverage-point.title: Finding Your Leverage Point
p:finding-your-leverage-point.blurb: Numbers, buffers, rules, information flow, goals, paradigm — the ladder of where change actually holds, walked through at Self, Dyad, and Skein scale.

c:position-speed-acceleration.title: Position, speed, acceleration
c:position-speed-acceleration.blurb: The second question. You never touch position directly; you apply a force, which is acceleration, and time integrates the rest. Why high-leverage work shows no visible movement for a long time.

c:coasting-vs-accelerating.title: Coasting vs. accelerating
c:coasting-vs-accelerating.blurb: Holding a speed already reached costs only enough to cancel drag; building it from zero costs far more, because one is maintaining existing momentum and the other is generating momentum that doesn't exist yet. Explains why people quit mid-build, mistaking the cost of construction for evidence of failure. Test: has this gotten easier, or have you just gotten used to how hard it is?

c:loop-period.title: Loop period
c:loop-period.blurb: A loop's natural period sets how long you need to have watched before honestly telling a trend from a stage; a fast loop announces itself, a slow one disguises itself as the ground you're standing on. A written log is the tool for this specifically, since memory doesn't span a slow loop's period the way a record can.

c:the-sacrifice-trap.title: The Sacrifice Trap
c:the-sacrifice-trap.blurb: Grind now, live later is a trade that never pays out. A meditation for the moment you catch yourself making it.

c:doubling-time.title: Doubling time
c:doubling-time.blurb: Seventy divided by the growth rate. Natural period tells you when a trend is readable; doubling time tells you when it becomes visible in position.

c:commitments-multiply-rather-than-add.title: Commitments multiply rather than add
c:commitments-multiply-rather-than-add.blurb: Each new one is carried in the presence of all the others, so cost scales with the pairs rather than the count. Setting a load and feeling it are different moments, and the first is cheap.

p:position-speed-acceleration.title: Position, Speed, Acceleration
p:position-speed-acceleration.blurb: The same three orders that describe motion describe a habit, a Dyad, or a Skein — and why real leverage often looks like nothing happening yet.

c:woven-self.title: The Woven Self
c:woven-self.blurb: The Third Thing pointed at the self.

c:atomic-composition.title: Atomic composition
c:atomic-composition.blurb: Electrons move constantly at no cost to identity (Numbers-level); neutrons are stable until they aren't, decaying on their own schedule if unprocessed (echoes the Compost Heap); protons require nuclear force to move at all, and moving them changes the element itself (Paradigm-level). A physical body for the claim that a self changes constantly at one cost and almost never at another.

c:naming-and-defusing.title: Naming and defusing
c:naming-and-defusing.blurb: The self-stories that feel like settled fact — "I always quit" — and the practice of catching them as patterns instead of verdicts.

c:felt-evaluation-as-machinery.title: Felt evaluation as machinery
c:felt-evaluation-as-machinery.blurb: Fast evaluation is not interference with choosing, it is how choosing terminates; damage it and decisions never resolve. Also the mechanical reason a Label works — it arrives pre-weighted on the felt channel before deliberation is consulted.

p:psychology-woven-self.title: The Psychology of the Woven Self
p:psychology-woven-self.blurb: The experiencing self, the remembering self, and the observing self — three research traditions converging on a self that was always assembled.

p:the-woven-self.title: The Woven Self
p:the-woven-self.blurb: The self is the hardest place to actually apply the Third Thing pillar — the one thing you'll never get to see from outside.

c:presence-as-a-channel-condition.title: Presence as a channel condition
c:presence-as-a-channel-condition.blurb: Not a virtue. The channel must carry signal before anything you send arrives as signal, which is why an accurate reading delivered to a closed channel lands as an attack. Presence makes understanding possible; understanding is what care is made of.

c:two-coupled-models.title: Two coupled models
c:two-coupled-models.blurb: A game builds one mental model indirectly through a feedback loop; a conversation builds two, each changing in response to the other. Ordinary conversation is two oscillators pulling into phase; acute distress narrows bandwidth, and there the asymmetry is real.

c:empathy-vs-sympathy.title: Empathy vs sympathy
c:empathy-vs-sympathy.blurb: Feeling *with* rather than *for*; the second creates distance while looking like closeness. Requires locating the feeling in yourself, which is why it costs something and why it is downstream of your own practice.

c:the-insight-asymmetry.title: The insight asymmetry
c:the-insight-asymmetry.blurb: People are biased toward believing they understand others better than others understand them. A taxonomy for reading people accelerates exactly that bias: the fluency is real and the confidence outruns it invisibly. You see about a tenth of a person; the rest is offered, not deduced.

p:presence.title: Presence
p:presence.blurb: A conversation is two people each building a model of the other while being modelled themselves — why an accurate reading lands as an attack until the other person can tell you're actually there.

c:sute-ishi-the-deliberate-release.title: Sute-ishi — the deliberate release
c:sute-ishi-the-deliberate-release.blurb: Letting go of something still saveable because holding it costs more than it is worth. Distinct from the Compost Heap, which recovers material from what already failed. The question: what am I still holding only because I have already spent on it?

c:action-before-motivation-and-the-test-.title: Action before motivation, and the test it enables
c:action-before-motivation-and-the-test-.blurb: Acting first generates wanting, reliably, for capacity problems. It does nothing for ownership problems. Seven days of honest action: capacity produces momentum, an owed thing stays exactly as flat.

c:the-three-legged-stall.title: The three-legged stall
c:the-three-legged-stall.blurb: Capacity, understanding, want; non-substitutable fixes; the test for the third leg is whether you look forward to starting or only to having finished.

p:the-stall.title: The Stall
p:the-stall.blurb: A stall has exactly three possible causes — capacity, understanding, or want — and each has its own fix that does not substitute for the others.

c:bottom-up-or-nothing.title: Bottom-up or nothing
c:bottom-up-or-nothing.blurb: A framework built on global forms arising without a designer cannot coherently acquire a central authority; it would refute itself in the act of organizing. Nobody reads you better than you read yourself; belonging is pride, never obligation; you are the captain of your own ship.

c:being-named-is-not-being-reduced.title: Being named is not being reduced
c:being-named-is-not-being-reduced.blurb: Pattern → Third Thing → real. The chain is the answer to hearing "you are a loop" as a demotion. The refused inference is the other one: you are X, therefore you must Y.

p:bottom-up-or-nothing.title: Bottom-Up or Nothing
p:bottom-up-or-nothing.blurb: Fractalism cannot have a central authority, the same way a circle cannot have corners — and the line between naming a pattern and handing someone a verdict.

c:two-senses-of-real.title: Two senses of "real"
c:two-senses-of-real.blurb: Structural realism (a Third Thing is real independent of anyone perceiving it — solidity, a floral electric field) and experiential realism (a feeling's occurrence is real simply because it's happening, separate from whether its content is true). Confusing the two is a major source of unnecessary internal struggle.

c:the-forward-chain-that-multiplies.title: The forward chain that multiplies
c:the-forward-chain-that-multiplies.blurb: A catastrophic story runs in individually plausible steps and compounds down to something far less likely than any step in it. Don't argue the ending; count the links.

p:naming-and-defusing.title: Naming and Defusing
p:naming-and-defusing.blurb: The self-stories that feel like settled fact — "I always quit" — and the practice of catching them as patterns instead of verdicts.

c:association-machine.title: The association machine
c:association-machine.blurb: A mind doesn't observe and separately interpret; it fuses the two, which is why a harsh self-judgment feels like fact rather than guess. Naming a self-story is the manual, effortful version of pulling that fusion back apart by hand.

c:capacity-to-steer.title: The capacity to steer
c:capacity-to-steer.blurb: A fast, reliable association is not automatically a beneficial one. Telling the two apart, then choosing to override a working pattern rather than simply ride it, is a real, non-default capacity — and the actual reason a practice is worth having at all.

c:the-skein.title: The Skein
c:the-skein.blurb: Real community, bound by repeated contact rather than a shared label.

c:the-braid.title: The Braid
c:the-braid.blurb: A Skein and a Banner fused; real substance carrying a visible name.

c:company-you-keep.title: The company you keep
c:company-you-keep.blurb: The popular version and the real mechanism.

p:reading-the-global-form.title: Reading the Global Form
p:reading-the-global-form.blurb: Three questions to run on any recurring occasion you already keep — including the uncomfortable one: does this map to a cautionary figure rather than an admirable one?

p:the-dyad.title: The Dyad
p:the-dyad.blurb: A Skein narrowed to exactly two people, woven completely enough to function as a single unit — and why complete doesn't automatically mean healthy.

p:the-skein.title: The Skein
p:the-skein.blurb: The difference between a community bound by real repeated contact and one bound only by a label — and the test that tells them apart.

c:beyond-telling.title: Beyond telling
c:beyond-telling.blurb: Why traditions with no contact converge.

c:compensatory-control.title: Compensatory control
c:compensatory-control.blurb: When agency feels threatened people reach for external structure as a substitute. Explains why a Banner feels like belonging, predicts Banner-drift as a shock risk rather than a growth risk, and gives the Salve and the Mask a shared root.

p:belief-systems-built.title: On Belief Systems That Know They're Built
p:belief-systems-built.blurb: Every belief system is constructed. The difference is honesty about it — and the difference between infecting someone and inoculating them.

c:fractal-resistance.title: Fractal Resistance
c:fractal-resistance.blurb: Being the honest variation inside a rigid structure.

p:fractal-resistance.title: Fractal Resistance, Practiced
p:fractal-resistance.blurb: Inside a system that resists change, be one honest, differently-behaving part — variation as immunity, not rebellion.

p:fractalism-collective.title: Fractalism and the Collective
p:fractalism-collective.blurb: History moves in loops at civilizational scale — and every large "we" is a Third Thing doing work face-to-face familiarity can't.

c:open-and-closed-boundaries.title: Open and closed boundaries
c:open-and-closed-boundaries.blurb: A closed boundary (judged by external behavior, not internal accuracy) is not a lesser Word — it's often the correct one, and the elegance test applies directly: the right boundary gives the most correct prediction for the least internal machinery the purpose actually needs. A closed boundary corrodes into a Label only once it's kept past the point it stops predicting anything, or opened only once a genuinely different purpose needs what's inside. The same act, in different language, as naming a scale.

c:word-vs-label.title: Word vs. Label
c:word-vs-label.blurb: Pulled toward something real, or pushed to produce an effect.

p:grammar-of-pattern.title: The Grammar of Pattern
p:grammar-of-pattern.blurb: The Loop Tongue's working vocabulary, plus the Word/Label test — is a term pulled toward something real, or pushed to produce a reaction?

c:three-kinds-of-knowing.title: Three kinds of knowing
c:three-kinds-of-knowing.blurb: Being told a pattern (the Loop-name, transmissible, cheap), having lived a pattern (its Tree, which can only be walked), and knowing which pattern you're currently inside (neither of the first two, and not produced by either). Scale-Tagging, the complex/complicated gate, and the two-pole check all serve the third.

c:a-stopped-pattern-has-no-pole.title: A stopped pattern has no pole
c:a-stopped-pattern-has-no-pole.blurb: Tending and Fraying describe the direction of a running pattern. Nothing running means nothing to read, which is a distinct answer from being zoomed in too far.

p:scale-tagging.title: Scale-Tagging
p:scale-tagging.blurb: Most arguments between people who agree are two descriptions of the same pattern at different scales. Name your zoom level before you speak.

c:the-banner.title: The Banner
c:the-banner.blurb: A shared label with nothing underneath it.

p:do-i-understand-you.title: Do I Understand You Well Enough?
p:do-i-understand-you.blurb: The single most practical sentence in the book, meant to be asked out loud before you assume you know what someone needs.

c:balance-is-a-wave.title: Balance is a wave
c:balance-is-a-wave.blurb: Balance is never stillness; it is continuous correction whose average looks like rest. Stopping the correction is a distinct failure from retreating early. If you can't see the work, that's your resolution, not the thing.

c:hornet-solar-cycle.title: The Oriental hornet's solar cycle
c:hornet-solar-cycle.blurb: A literal, not metaphorical, instance of tide-based homeostasis: solar energy harvested by the cuticle, activity correlated with sunlight intensity, the same reinforcing-then-balancing rhythm already claimed for the tide, running in a real insect.

c:reinforcing-balancing.title: Reinforcing and balancing rhythm
c:reinforcing-balancing.blurb: Fractalism's genesis story: no voice speaking from outside the system — only a small pattern, repeating, until repetition became a universe.

c:order-is-not-free.title: Order is not free
c:order-is-not-free.blurb: Any arrangement is one of an enormous number, nearly all less organized, so holding one costs continuously. The caution that must travel with it: the one-directional law applies to closed systems, and nothing in a life is one. The honest form is that nothing which has stopped being paid for stays where you left it.

p:reading-your-own-cycle.title: Reading Your Own Cycle
p:reading-your-own-cycle.blurb: Reinforcing loops amplify; balancing loops correct back toward a middle — and everything that survives runs both at once, like a tide.

c:loop.title: Loop
c:loop.blurb: A repeated cycle where output becomes the next input.

c:signed-loop-polarity.title: Signed-loop polarity
c:signed-loop-polarity.blurb: Every link in a loop carries a sign (does more of the cause produce more or less of the effect); count the negative links, and an even count (including zero) is reinforcing, an odd count is balancing. The actual arithmetic underneath the ↻ and ⤸ marks — derivable, not a judgment call.

p:daily-practices.title: The Daily Practices
p:daily-practices.blurb: Four short practices that carry the daily weight: the breath, Tree-Gazing, Naming the Loop, and Seeding — each with the mechanism explained.

p:sketching-a-loop.title: Sketching a Loop
p:sketching-a-loop.blurb: Four marks, learnable in under a minute, sketchable on a napkin mid-conversation: →, ↻, ⤸, and [ ].

p:the-mathematics.title: The Mathematics
p:the-mathematics.blurb: The chaos game, done properly: randomness and determinism converging on the identical structure, checkable with a pencil.

c:tree.title: Tree
c:tree.blurb: The branching record a Loop's name compresses.

c:core-mantra.title: The core mantra
c:core-mantra.blurb: *You feel a line. You are a loop. You build a tree.*.

p:the-loop-runs-you.title: The Loop Runs You Right Now
p:the-loop-runs-you.blurb: The self is not a thing you have. It's a pattern you're running — and a thing built by repetition can be rebuilt by repetition.

p:the-second-pass.title: The Second Pass
p:the-second-pass.blurb: Any claim worth making twice is worth making once forward and once as a loop — the habit that turns a villain story into a shared pattern.

p:why-lines-break-loops.title: Why Lines Break Loops
p:why-lines-break-loops.blurb: A sentence has an ending. A loop doesn't. Why ordinary language quietly deletes the part of a pattern where the leverage lives.

c:seven-iterations.title: The Seven Iterations
c:seven-iterations.blurb: Fractalism's genesis story: no voice speaking from outside the system — only a small pattern, repeating, until repetition became a universe.

p:group-practice.title: Group Practice
p:group-practice.blurb: A simple structure for practicing with witnesses: share one loop, offer one leverage point, close with a seed.

p:mantras.title: The Mantras, Prayers, and Meditations
p:mantras.blurb: The full text of every mantra, prayer, and meditation — for daily use, alone or in groups.

p:where-it-comes-from.title: Where It Comes From — The Seven Iterations
p:where-it-comes-from.blurb: Fractalism's genesis story: no voice speaking from outside the system — only a small pattern, repeating, until repetition became a universe.

c:not-self-help.title: Not self-help
c:not-self-help.blurb: This belief system tells you it was built — on purpose, and this isn't self-help or organization-building. It's a rising tide, not a ledger.

c:this-is-not-care.title: This is not care
c:this-is-not-care.blurb: The framework is a way of looking, not treatment. A trained person is present, accountable, and adjusts as you change, which no book is. Understanding a pattern is not being relieved of it.

p:a-word-on-belief.title: A Word on Belief Itself
p:a-word-on-belief.blurb: This belief system tells you it was built — on purpose, and this isn't self-help or organization-building. It's a rising tide, not a ledger.

p:onboarding.title: Start Here: The One-Week Onboarding
p:onboarding.blurb: Seven days, one small thing per day. Don't adopt everything at once — that would be the exact mistake the whole book warns against.

c:why-a-turning-has-an-aim-rather-than-t.title: Why a Turning has an aim rather than two poles
c:why-a-turning-has-an-aim-rather-than-t.blurb: Poles describe the direction of a found pattern; intent describes what a made thing is for. A designed practice fails by drifting into performance or obligation, not by pointing the other way.

c:what-actually-bonds-a-group.title: What actually bonds a group
c:what-actually-bonds-a-group.blurb: Not synchrony. A loop running Tending between people, where each pass leaves both parties with more than they brought. Doing something together opens the loop; which way it points decides whether it builds.

p:what-a-turning-is.title: What a Turning Is
p:what-a-turning-is.blurb: A shared, recurring occasion aimed at a Global Form that hasn't finished arriving — not a commemoration, because this practice has no history to commemorate and won't invent one.

c:why-practices-work.title: Why the practices work
c:why-practices-work.blurb: The experiencing self, the remembering self, and the observing self — three research traditions converging on a self that was always assembled.

c:satisfaction-is-logarithmic.title: Satisfaction is logarithmic
c:satisfaction-is-logarithmic.blurb: Equal increments of felt gain require multiplicative increases in input, so a reinforcing loop and its perception are inverse curves and holding felt gain constant requires endless acceleration. Most of the available value sits early.

p:flow-reward.title: Flow, Reward, and Why Practice Works
p:flow-reward.blurb: Why something this simple produces a felt sense of meaning: challenge-skill balance, hedonic adaptation, and reward that doesn't degrade.

c:creative-work-as-compost.title: Creative work as compost
c:creative-work-as-compost.blurb: Failure isn't waste — it's the substrate the next attempt grows out of. How creative work actually gets sustained.

p:the-compost-heap.title: The Compost Heap
p:the-compost-heap.blurb: Failure isn't waste — it's the substrate the next attempt grows out of. How creative work actually gets sustained.

c:suffering-as-usable-material.title: Suffering as usable material
c:suffering-as-usable-material.blurb: Self, Dyad, and Skein were never separate — and the whole practice was always closer to a rising tide than a ledger.

p:closing-the-loop.title: Closing the Loop
p:closing-the-loop.blurb: Self, Dyad, and Skein were never separate — and the whole practice was always closer to a rising tide than a ledger.

c:weaving.title: Weaving
c:weaving.blurb: Reading a situation from four distances. Progressive reveal is the core technique.

p:reading-honestly.title: Reading Honestly
p:reading-honestly.blurb: A Weaving describes a pattern; it does not predict an outcome. The genuinely useful reading is often the uncomfortable one.

p:tending-and-fraying.title: Tending and Fraying
p:tending-and-fraying.blurb: Every Third carries its healthy expression and its own documented flaw. Tending is not good news, and Fraying is not bad news.

p:the-four-point-weaving.title: The Four-Point Weaving
p:the-four-point-weaving.blurb: The standard form: one card per ring — Self, Dyad, Skein, Culture — with no privileged first card, and the rings don't have to agree.

p:the-rings.title: The Rings, Not the Row
p:the-rings.blurb: A Weaving is laid out as nested rings, never a row — Self, Dyad, Skein, and Culture, four nested resolutions of one situation, not four chapters of a story.

p:the-single-pull.title: The Single Pull
p:the-single-pull.blurb: The lightest form — one Third drawn at random, read loosely for the day ahead. A daily practice, not a consultation.

p:weaving-for-another.title: Weaving for Another
p:weaving-for-another.blurb: Reveal one card at a time, and fold the other person's response into how you read the next one — the mechanism that makes a reading personal.

p:weaving-limits.title: What a Weaving Cannot Show
p:weaving-limits.blurb: Diagnostic, never prescriptive — and never a substitute for an actual conversation with an actual person.

p:what-a-weaving-is.title: What a Weaving Is
p:what-a-weaving-is.blurb: A structured way of looking at one situation from several fixed angles at once — because a single vantage was never going to show you the whole shape.

c:the-full-unravelling-as-a-derivation.title: The Full Unravelling, as a derivation
c:the-full-unravelling-as-a-derivation.blurb: Draw two Self-Kin and stop. Their fusion names exactly one Dyad-Kin; that pairs upward to a Skein-Kin, and once more to a Culture-Kin. One situation at four depths, each accounting for the one below, rather than four angles side by side.

p:the-full-unravelling.title: The Full Unravelling
p:the-full-unravelling.blurb: Reserved for the large, rare questions — the whole relevant portion of the deck at once, laid out slowly and sat with honestly.

c:weather-climate-terrain.title: Weather, Climate, Terrain
c:weather-climate-terrain.blurb: The three speeds at which any drawn figure can be read: now, this season, the shape underneath a life. Distinct from ring position, which names how many people a pattern runs through rather than how long it has been running. Distress reliably makes Weather feel like Terrain.

p:weather-climate-terrain.title: Weather, Climate, Terrain
p:weather-climate-terrain.blurb: A ring tells you how many people a pattern runs through. It doesn't tell you how long it's been running — so every card gets asked a second question, at three speeds.

c:why-this-is-a-deck-and-not-a-divinatio.title: Why this is a deck and not a divination
c:why-this-is-a-deck-and-not-a-divinatio.blurb: The form is borrowed from tarot and the three changes are load-bearing: the cards describe rather than foretell, no card is fortunate, and the randomness exists to supply the angle you would not have chosen.

p:the-deck.title: The Deck
p:the-deck.blurb: The full working deck: fifty-two drawable figures across five kinships, each carrying two readings — plus one figure that's never drawn at all.

c:the-spark.title: The Spark
c:the-spark.blurb: What comes out feeds what goes in next. Momentum that compounds, whether it is building something or burning it down.

c:the-tide.title: The Tide
c:the-tide.blurb: The pull back toward a setpoint. It gives a system the recovery it needs, and it can also call the retreat before the work is done.

c:the-mark.title: The Mark
c:the-mark.blurb: Judging everything against a reference point. Without one you can't judge at all; kept too long, it rules a world that has moved on.

c:the-salve.title: The Salve
c:the-salve.blurb: Reaching first for whatever eases the symptom. A good stopgap buys time to build the real fix; a permanent one wears away the ability it replaced.

c:the-nearest-light.title: The Nearest Light
c:the-nearest-light.blurb: Trusting whatever reaches you first. Sometimes the latest signal really is the truest; sometimes the most vivid thing only feels the most common.

c:the-keepsake.title: The Keepsake
c:the-keepsake.blurb: Remembering an experience by its peak and its ending. It makes a life tellable as a story, at the cost of a record that doesn't match what was lived.

c:the-easier-door.title: The Easier Door
c:the-easier-door.blurb: Quietly swapping a hard question for an easier one. It's how hard questions get answered at all, and how confident answers get given to questions nobody asked.

c:the-mask.title: The Mask
c:the-mask.blurb: Holding to a story about yourself even against the evidence. That conviction makes commitment possible, until it becomes a self you can't see around.

c:the-mirror.title: The Mirror
c:the-mirror.blurb: Taking your shape from whoever is in the room. A self truly built through relationship, or no position of your own once the audience changes.

c:the-namer.title: The Namer
c:the-namer.blurb: Speaking as though the words will build what follows, because they do. Language that makes something real, sometimes something real that works against you.

c:the-riverbed.title: The Riverbed
c:the-riverbed.blurb: Shaping your surroundings so one action becomes the easy one. It takes willpower out of the equation, and leaves you stranded when the surroundings change.

c:the-gardener.title: The Gardener
c:the-gardener.blurb: Returning your attention, again and again, to one thing among many. Whatever you attend to grows, including whatever you keep confirming.

c:escalation.title: Escalation
c:escalation.blurb: Two people each answering the other with a little more. It can lift both to their best, or lock them in an arms race neither chose and neither can leave.

c:the-standoff.title: The Standoff
c:the-standoff.blurb: Two people each easing back and waiting on the other. Room given without forcing, or a stalemate both of them call patience.

c:the-pairing.title: The Pairing
c:the-pairing.blurb: One person drives while the other steadies. A real division of labor, or a standing resentment between the accelerator and the brake.

c:filling-the-gap.title: Filling the Gap
c:filling-the-gap.blurb: Supplying what someone else thinks and feels from your own assumptions. It saves checking every time, until you're relating to someone who isn't there.

c:the-shared-story.title: The Shared Story
c:the-shared-story.blurb: A memory two people build and keep together. It binds them to something real, or to an account of an event neither of them actually had.

c:the-echo.title: The Echo
c:the-echo.blurb: Two people each taking their shape from the other. Genuinely formed by each other, or a pair with no fixed position anywhere between them.

c:the-naming-contest.title: The Naming Contest
c:the-naming-contest.blurb: Two people each trying to name what is happening between them. A vocabulary built together, or a duel of framings where naming replaces resolving.

c:the-arrangement.title: The Arrangement
c:the-arrangement.blurb: Each person shaping the other's surroundings instead of asking directly. The right thing made easy, or two people quietly managing each other.

c:the-tested-price.title: The Tested Price
c:the-tested-price.blurb: Naming the terms and checking them before agreeing. A deal both sides can trust, or terms accepted untested, or testing that never ends.

c:the-inner-circle.title: The Inner Circle
c:the-inner-circle.blurb: A group whose shared language makes its work fast. The same fluency can become a wall against everyone outside it.

c:watering-another.title: Watering Another
c:watering-another.blurb: Attention that keeps returning to someone, and grows what it lands on. It can grow the best in them, or whatever you've already decided they are.

c:answering-for.title: Answering For
c:answering-for.blurb: One person keeps supplying what the other needs to know. Expertise given generously, or help that stops them ever developing their own.

c:the-guard.title: The Guard
c:the-guard.blurb: A boundary held between two people. It protects something real, or hardens into armor that blocks the connection it was protecting.

c:reading-the-room.title: Reading the Room
c:reading-the-room.blurb: Reading another person's state from what they stir in you. Emotion used as honest information, or your own reaction mistaken for theirs.

c:connection-first.title: Connection First
c:connection-first.blurb: Leading with warmth before any content. Warmth that lets hard information land, or warmth standing in for having anything to say.

c:the-rising-bar.title: The Rising Bar
c:the-rising-bar.blurb: Standards between two people that keep ratcheting up. They climb as real capacity grows, or climb past the point where anything is ever enough.

c:the-sliding-floor.title: The Sliding Floor
c:the-sliding-floor.blurb: Standards between two people that keep easing down. An honest adjustment to changed conditions, or erosion in steps too small to notice.

c:typecasting.title: Typecasting
c:typecasting.blurb: Seeing someone as one kind of person until they become it. It can call real capability out of them, or lock them into a single role.

c:gaming-the-terms.title: Gaming the Terms
c:gaming-the-terms.blurb: Keeping to the letter of an agreement while finding the easy way through it. Creative slack in a bad deal, or its purpose quietly hollowed out.

c:the-unbridged-gap.title: The Unbridged Gap
c:the-unbridged-gap.blurb: Deep fluency on one side that the other side can't reach. Skill that comes from real depth, or an inability to picture a mind without your context.

c:held-silence.title: Held Silence
c:held-silence.blurb: A group that knows something and doesn't say it. Discretion that lets it survive ordinary friction, or a truth nobody can be the first to name.

c:transmission-drift.title: Transmission Drift
c:transmission-drift.blurb: A story that changes a little with every teller. It survives by adapting to each one, or drifts free of what it started as.

c:the-faithful-chain.title: The Faithful Chain
c:the-faithful-chain.blurb: A craft handed from person to person, each taught by someone who was taught. Skill kept intact across people who never met, and dependence kept intact with it.

c:first-arriver-lock-in.title: First-Arriver Lock-In
c:first-arriver-lock-in.blurb: A group rewarding whatever already works, so the early winners keep winning. Merit rewarded, or whoever arrived first entrenched regardless of it.

c:the-shared-pot.title: The Shared Pot
c:the-shared-pot.blurb: A resource a whole group draws on freely. Trust that makes keeping accounts unnecessary, or a common that nobody is placed to protect.

c:the-reputation.title: The Reputation
c:the-reputation.blurb: The role a group comes to count on you to play. It lets them rely on you, and because they wrote it, it can be hard to step out of.

c:the-sagging-floor.title: The Sagging Floor
c:the-sagging-floor.blurb: A group's expectations lowering together, one reasonable step at a time. A sensible adjustment to real conditions, or standards eroding while everyone feels fine.

c:the-hall-of-mirrors.title: The Hall of Mirrors
c:the-hall-of-mirrors.blurb: A group where everyone takes their shape from everyone else. Real responsiveness to itself, or no independent position left anywhere in it.

c:second-order-design.title: Second-Order Design
c:second-order-design.blurb: A group shaping the conditions that shape its members. Outcomes richer than anyone could have authored, or ones nobody intended or wanted.

c:the-only-road.title: The Only Road
c:the-only-road.blurb: One person who is the only bridge between two groups. They connect worlds that would otherwise never meet, and losing them cuts those worlds apart.

c:the-shared-name.title: The Shared Name
c:the-shared-name.blurb: A name that gathers vast numbers of people into a "we". It can bind people who are genuinely connected, or people with nothing underneath the name.

c:proxy-detachment.title: Proxy Detachment
c:proxy-detachment.blurb: A measure standing in for something too large to see directly. It makes a vast system legible, until it is optimized so hard it stops tracking what it measured.

c:policy-resistance.title: Policy Resistance
c:policy-resistance.blurb: A whole system pushing back against every push. Stability no single actor could have imposed, or everyone straining harder while nothing moves.

c:the-long-cycle.title: The Long Cycle
c:the-long-cycle.blurb: Growth that compounds across generations. It builds for a long time, and past a threshold the same mechanism consumes what it built.

c:the-received-world.title: The Received World
c:the-received-world.blurb: What a culture hands down without the reasons attached. Knowledge that works without needing explaining, or practice hollowed of why it ever existed.

c:the-slow-hand.title: The Slow Hand
c:the-slow-hand.blurb: Change too slow for any single life to watch. Continuity that outlasts every turbulence, or a slow shift mistaken for permanence.

c:independent-convergence.title: Independent Convergence
c:independent-convergence.blurb: The same answer found twice by people with no contact. Real evidence when no path connects them, or shared bias mistaken for confirmation.

c:the-standing-account.title: The Standing Account
c:the-standing-account.blurb: A civilization tracking itself through a number so it can steer. It can let a society see itself well enough to build deliberately, or keep steering by a number that stopped tracking the thing while the thing is spent.

c:second-nature.title: Second Nature
c:second-nature.blurb: Structure built up so gradually and so well-fitted that nobody has to attend to it anymore. It can free a civilization to build on top of what already works, or get mistaken for the given world rather than a made one, and go unopposed for being invisible.

c:the-set-course.title: The Set Course
c:the-set-course.blurb: A direction set early enough that everything downstream gets built on top of it. It can let generations build on a shared foundation, or lock a course in place, set by people no longer here to argue with.
